reason: The text contains only three named individual characters: Moses (מֹשֶׁה), Aaron (אַהֲרֹן), and Pharaoh (פַּרְעֹה). Moses and Aaron are portrayed as divine agents who perform miracles and receive direct instructions from God—they are prophets fulfilling a divine mission. Pharaoh is presented as a ruler and antagonist whose heart is hardened by God. While the text references various groups of people (Israelites, Egyptians, servants, taskmasters, magicians), these are collective references without individual names. The three named characters are all figures of religious, political, or cosmic significance rather than ordinary people.
